workflow.decision: Question whether object publication and companion policy initialization form one protected transition. The reported incomplete state and guard failure motivate a visibility-invariant hypothesis; inspect the creation and policy-reader relationship rather than assuming the normal completed state applies throughout. The unresolved questions are the consumer's missing-state rule and the actual atomicity and synchronization boundary.

Question whether a presentation-purpose length adjustment preserves a security encoder's guarantee. The author describes escaping followed by truncation and reports changed syntax at consumption; compare guarantees across the ordered transformations, not merely the presence of an escape call. Final representation, encoded-unit integrity and actual consumer reachability remain independent validation questions.

limitations: This is an educational CTF writeup from 2015, not evidence of a current production vulnerability or a general runtime default.
The guard failure, changed parsing and challenge outcomes are author reports. No source execution, target interaction or independent reproduction was performed.
The race discussion does not provide state traces, attempt counts, measured timing or a transaction/isolation analysis; publication visibility and practical scheduling remain unresolved.
The prose illustrates the transformation order but does not establish a complete parser/configuration matrix, paired benign controls or a repaired implementation. No remediation result is claimed.

An additional file-inclusion section appears beyond the two mechanisms named in the title. Its target-specific restrictions and exploit composition are omitted rather than promoted to a separate operational method.
The retained lessons overlap existing publication and transformation-order guidance. Candidate additions are narrow review prompts, not claims of novelty or final library acceptance.

candidate_additions.guidance: When an object and its companion policy state are initialized separately, review what a reader concludes from missing policy state. Treat visibility before policy completion as an invariant hypothesis even when neither reader nor writer uses a stale value; require evidence of the actual atomicity boundary before claiming a race.

Include presentation-purpose truncation and formatting among security-relevant writers when the changed value is reused by a sensitive consumer. A display-oriented reason for mutation does not prove the mutation is confined to output rendering.

For length-changing operations after encoding, review whether complete encoded units and delimiter meaning survive to the final consumer. Distinguish a bound on length from a guarantee of syntactic safety, and retain an unresolved classification when final consumption or effective parser rules are unknown.
